input.quote: provided that the payment by PB to SFJ of the amounts specified as being payable upon a given termination in Section 14.2 shall be in lieu of any claim for damages that SFJ may have arising out of or in connection with the circumstances that formed the basis for such termination.
input.rationale: Section 14.4.2 characterises the Section 14.2 termination sums as amounts payable by PB "in lieu of any claim for damages" — liquidated amounts payable by us, the Customer. The formulas are punitive rather than compensatory: 300% of Development Costs on SFJ's termination for our breach (14.2.1), on our at-will termination (14.2.2), on bankruptcy termination (14.2.5.2) and in the safety cases (14.2.7); 150% on Change of Control or compliance-breach termination (14.2.6, 14.2.8.1); and Development Costs plus 25% per annum where SFJ merely disagrees with a JSC decision (14.2.10). That is at or beyond walk-away territory and far outside the fallback ceiling. We do not flag the Section 6.7 Buy-Out Payments (an elective prepayment right benefiting us) or Section 6.4 default interest. Deleting every 14.2 formula to reach the preferred no-LD position would require collateral rewrites of the funding economics, so we target the fallback with one edit to the exclusive-remedy proviso, which already opens "Notwithstanding anything herein to the contrary". The revised proviso caps the payment at three months of Development Costs — the Agreement has no periodic "fees", and Development Costs is the defined, ascertainable running-spend base (the SFJ Interim Management Fee is a redacted lump sum limited to the Interim Period) — and makes it the sole amount payable on termination "whether as liquidated damages or consideration for the Trial Data Package", so the retained 14.2 purchase-consideration wording, the 14.2.2/14.2.10 offsets for amounts "previously paid ... pursuant to this Section" and the Section 11.1.1.4 purchase mechanic all continue to operate against the capped fee. Post-approval Approval Payments, which are not termination amounts, are untouched.

proposal.summary: Cap PB's termination payment at an early-termination fee equal to three months of Development Costs, as the sole amount payable whether as damages or as Trial Data Package consideration
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 14.4.2 currently makes the Section 14.2 termination sums (up to 300% of Development Costs) liquidated amounts payable by us in lieu of SFJ's damages claim. We have capped them at a single early-termination fee equal to three months of Development Costs and made it the sole amount payable on termination, whether characterised as liquidated damages or as consideration for the Trial Data Package, so the retained Section 14.2 formulas and the Section 11.1.1.4 purchase mechanic conform.

ops.oldText: provided that the payment by PB to SFJ of the amounts specified as being payable upon a given termination in Section 14.2 shall be in lieu of any claim for damages that SFJ may have arising out of or in connection with the circumstances that formed the basis for such termination.
ops.newText: provided that the sole amount payable by PB upon a given termination in Section 14.2, whether as liquidated damages or consideration for the Trial Data Package, shall be an early-termination fee not exceeding Development Costs paid or incurred by SFJ during the three months preceding such termination, in lieu of any claim for damages that SFJ may have arising out of or in connection with the circumstances that formed the basis for such termination.
